questions.question: The S.I. unit of electric charge is the
questions.explanation: The S.I. unit of electric charge is the coulomb (C). One coulomb is the charge transported by a steady current of one ampere in one second.

questions.question: A charge of 1.6 × 10<sup>-19</sup>C is equivalent to the charge on
questions.explanation: The elementary charge has magnitude e = 1.6 × 10-19 C. An electron carries charge −e, while a proton carries +e. The magnitude matches the charge on one electron.

questions.question: The charge on an electron is
questions.explanation: An electron has a negative charge of −1.6 × 10-19 C.

questions.question: The quantization of charge means that charge exists in
questions.explanation: Quantization of charge means charge exists only in discrete amounts given by Q = ne, where n is an integer and e = 1.6 × 10-19 C.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a method of charging a body?
questions.explanation: The three methods of charging a body are friction, induction, and conduction. Radiation is not a charging method.

questions.question: When a glass rod is rubbed with silk, the rod becomes
questions.explanation: When glass is rubbed with silk, glass loses electrons to silk. Loss of electrons leaves the glass rod positively charged.

questions.question: When an ebonite rod is rubbed with fur, the rod becomes
questions.explanation: When ebonite is rubbed with fur, ebonite gains electrons from fur. Gain of electrons leaves the ebonite rod negatively charged.

questions.question: The law of conservation of charge states that charge can neither be
questions.explanation: The law of conservation of charge states that electric charge can neither be created nor destroyed; it can only be transferred from one body to another.

questions.question: Two point charges of +2μC and +8μC are separated by a distance of 0.3m. The force between them is
questions.explanation: Both charges are positive (like charges). Like charges repel each other.

questions.question: Coulomb's law states that the force between two point charges is directly proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the
options: square of the distance between them
cube of the distance between them
questions.explanation: Coulomb's law: F ∝ q1q2 and F ∝ 1/r2, so F = kq1q2/r2.

questions.question: The force between two charges of 1C each separated by 1m in vacuum is
questions.explanation: F = kq1q2/r2 = (9 × 109 × 1 × 1)/12 = 9 × 109 N.

questions.question: The permittivity of free space ε<sub>0</sub> has the value
questions.explanation: The permittivity of free space is ε0 = 8.85 × 10-12 C2 N-1 m-2.

questions.question: If the distance between two point charges is doubled, the force between them becomes
questions.explanation: F ∝ 1/r2. If r is doubled, force becomes 1/(2)2 = 1/4 of its original value.

questions.question: If the distance between two point charges is halved, the force between them becomes
questions.explanation: F ∝ 1/r2. If r is halved, force becomes 1/(1/2)2 = 4 times its original value.

questions.question: Two charges of +3μC and −3μC are separated by 0.2m. The force between them is
questions.explanation: Unlike charges (positive and negative) attract each other.

questions.question: The electric field intensity at a point is defined as the force per unit
questions.explanation: Electric field intensity (E) is defined as the force per unit positive charge: E = F/q.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of electric field intensity is
questions.explanation: E = F/q, so unit = N/C = N C-1.

questions.question: The electric field intensity at a distance r from a point charge Q is given by
questions.explanation: The electric field due to a point charge is E = kQ/r2.

questions.question: A charge of 2μC is placed in an electric field of intensity 5 × 10<sup>4</sup>NC<sup>-1</sup>. The force on the charge is
questions.explanation: F = qE = (2 × 10-6) × (5 × 104) = 0.1 N.

questions.question: The electric field lines due to an isolated positive point charge
questions.explanation: Electric field lines due to a positive charge point radially outward.

questions.question: Electric field lines due to an isolated negative point charge
questions.explanation: Electric field lines due to a negative charge point radially inward.

questions.question: Electric field lines are always
questions.explanation: Electric field lines are always perpendicular to the surface of a conductor.

questions.question: Electric field lines never
questions.explanation: Electric field lines never intersect each other because at any point the field has only one direction.

questions.question: The electric potential at a distance r from a point charge Q is given by
questions.explanation: The electric potential due to a point charge is V = kQ/r.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of electric potential is
questions.explanation: The S.I. unit of electric potential is the volt (V).

questions.question: The work done in moving a charge of 2C through a potential difference of 10V is
questions.explanation: W = qV = 2 × 10 = 20 J.

questions.question: The electric potential energy between two point charges q<sub>1</sub> and q<sub>2</sub> separated by distance r is
questions.explanation: The electric potential energy is U = kq1q2/r.

questions.question: An equipotential surface is a surface on which
questions.explanation: An equipotential surface is a surface on which the electric potential is constant.

questions.question: The electric potential at a point due to a positive charge is
questions.explanation: The potential due to a positive charge is positive.

questions.question: The electric potential at a point due to a negative charge is
questions.explanation: The potential due to a negative charge is negative.

questions.question: A capacitor of capacitance 10μF is charged to a potential difference of 100V. The charge stored is
questions.explanation: Q = CV = (10 × 10-6) × 100 = 1 × 10-3 C.

questions.question: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor is directly proportional to the
questions.explanation: C = ε0A/d, so C is directly proportional to the area of the plates.

questions.question: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor is inversely proportional to the
questions.explanation: C = ε0A/d, so C is inversely proportional to the distance between the plates.

questions.question: Three capacitors of 2μF each are connected in series. The effective capacitance is
Three capacitors of 2μF each are connected in parallel. The effective capacitance is
questions.explanation: For parallel: C = 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 μF.

questions.question: The energy stored in a capacitor of capacitance C charged to potential difference V is
questions.explanation: The energy stored is E = ½CV2.

questions.question: The energy stored in a 5μF capacitor charged to 200V is
questions.explanation: E = ½CV2 = ½ × (5 × 10-6) × (200)2 = 0.1 J.

questions.question: The electric flux through a closed surface is proportional to the
questions.explanation: By Gauss's law, electric flux through a closed surface is proportional to the charge enclosed.

questions.question: Gauss's law states that the total electric flux through a closed surface is equal to the
questions.explanation: Gauss's law: Φ = Q/ε0.

questions.question: A charge of +2μC is placed at the centre of a cube. The electric flux through one face of the cube is
questions.explanation: Total flux = Q/ε0. For a cube, flux through one face = Q/(6ε0).

questions.question: A charged conductor has all its charge on the
questions.explanation: In a charged conductor, all charge resides on the exterior surface.

questions.question: The electric field inside a hollow charged conductor is
questions.explanation: The electric field inside a hollow charged conductor is zero.

questions.question: The electric potential inside a hollow charged conductor is
options: equal to the potential on the surface
greater than the potential on the surface
less than the potential on the surface
questions.explanation: The electric potential inside a hollow charged conductor is equal to the potential on the surface.

questions.question: An electroscope is used to
questions.explanation: An electroscope is used to detect electric charge.

questions.question: When a negatively charged rod is brought near the cap of an uncharged electroscope, the leaves
questions.explanation: A negatively charged rod induces a positive charge on the cap and negative charge on the leaves. Like charges on leaves cause them to diverge.

questions.question: When a positively charged rod is brought near the cap of a positively charged electroscope, the leaves
questions.explanation: The positively charged rod repels positive charge onto the leaves, increasing their divergence.

questions.question: The process of charging a body without physical contact is called
questions.explanation: Induction is the process of charging a body without physical contact.

questions.question: Lightning is caused by
questions.explanation: Lightning is caused by both friction between clouds and air and the accumulation of charges in clouds.

questions.question: The electric field intensity due to a point charge is directly proportional to the
questions.explanation: E = kQ/r2, so E is directly proportional to the charge Q.

questions.question: Two point charges of +4μC and +9μC are separated by a distance of 0.6m. The force between them is
questions.explanation: F = kq1q2/r2 = (9 × 109 × 4 × 10-6 × 9 × 10-6)/(0.6)2 = 0.9 N.
